message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a weekday and is surrounded by a weekend, giving you at least three consecutive days off.)

| Date range | Holiday(s) | Notes |
|------------|------------|-------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day (Sunday) | Observed on Monday, Jan 2. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, BC, SK, MB) | Third Monday in February (Feb 20). |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday (Friday) | All provinces observe Good Friday. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day (Monday) | All provinces observe Victoria Day. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (Saturday) | Observed on Monday, Jul 3. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day (Monday) | All provinces observe Labour Day. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving (Monday) | All provinces observe Thanksgiving. |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day (Saturday) | Observed on Monday, Nov 13. |
| **Dec 23–27** | Christmas (Mon) & Boxing Day (Tue) | Christmas on Monday, Dec 25; Boxing Day on Tuesday, Dec 26 (observed on Dec 27). |

> **Provinces with additional holidays that create long weekends in 2023**  
> • **New Brunswick** – Family Day on Feb 20 (same as above).  
> • **Quebec** – No extra long‑weekend holidays beyond the federal ones listed.  
> • **Other provinces** – No additional long‑weekend holidays in 2023.

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app! If you need the exact dates for a specific province (e.g., “Family Day” in New Brunswick or “St. Patrick’s Day” in any province that observes it), let me know.
